scores.evidence: Problem, users and scope are clear and mostly consistent. PRD §1-3 give the problem, the two stages and the non-goals. README.md lines 41-52 are a measured-vs-assumed table that is better than most pilot proposals: 17/17 and 15-16/17 are labelled measured on synthetic fixtures; 984 820 tokens is labelled Haiku-era; current-routing usage is shown as 'Not yet measured'; EUR 38-40 per brief and the 50-minute target are labelled assumption and target; 210 h / EUR 3 990-4 200 is shown as arithmetic on assumptions, and the document says openly that PRD §10's EUR 5-6k does not follow from its own inputs. docs/COST_MODEL.md §4 reconciles the same number, and every figure carries an era banner (lines 3-9). Supersessions of the frozen PRD are recorded rather than hidden: docs/OPERATING_DECISIONS.md 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-22 cover creative delivery and data declaration; TIERS.md lines 6-10 and 16 carry the routing note; SCORECARD.md §3 says the creative promotion criterion is replaced. Tier reports 5-7 each end with explicit 'not claimed' boundaries (tier_5 lines 43-49, tier_6 50-66, tier_7 47-66), and SCORECARD.md §3 has a 'Value hypothesis for the Tier 5-7 agency layer' table marking every hypothesis Assumed. I checked the claims against code and artifacts: pytest gives 948 passed, 7 skipped, 48 xfailed, matching README line 52. A grep of README, docs, pilot docs, WALKTHROUGH, START_HERE and the tier reports finds no pilot-cost, investment, break-even or payback figure. As a managing director I can see the return floor but not what I am putting in to get it, and the pilot does not test the value the documents themselves call the real prize.
defects: The return has no cost side. No document states what the pilot costs the agency: hours over 4 weeks for the roughly 10 roles in ROLES.md (sponsor, DPO, operator/AI specialist, 2 champions, 2 leads, bilingual reviewer, traffic, creative lead), plus seats or usage. So the EUR 4.0-4.2k/yr floor (COST_MODEL.md §4) cannot be weighed against anything, and no break-even is given. A grep for break-even, pilot cost, investment and payback across the evidence set finds nothing.

The capacity-returned formula overstates net return. SCORECARD.md §3 line 47 and COST_MODEL.md §4 count only account-lead minutes, (120 - 50) x 180 / 60. The Tier 5-7 layer adds minutes from the bilingual attester, traffic, creative lead, champion and operator. SCORECARD.md §7 records total_team_min but gives it no baseline and no target, and the §3 value-hypothesis table lists 'Cost it adds' without netting it out anywhere.

The main value claim is not tested by the pilot. PRD §10 and COST_MODEL.md line 130 say returned hours 'only fund the pilot' and that the case rests on the variance floor and downstream rework. SCORECARD.md §3 marks downstream measures 'Not pilot-scored' with the baseline 'OWNER TO CONFIRM', and GO_LIVE_DECISIONS.md D-19 defers it to quarter 1. So the go/no-go can at most confirm the floor the documents call secondary.

TIERS.md contradicts itself. The status line (lines 6-8) says 'No Tier 8 is authorised; the owner's whole-project review loop ... is not a tier', yet the same file has a 'Tier 8' section with a green DoD (lines 117-143), and README line 81 and commit 1aaa560 ('tier-8: ...') record Tier 8.

OPERATING_TERMS.md has stale citations. §b and §e cite 'docs/TIERS.md line 55' for the enterprise-API note, which is now line 62 (line 55 is a Tier 3 checklist item). §e cites 'CLAUDE.md ... line 55', which is now '## Workflow'. §c cites 'the measured $2.25 (docs/COST_MODEL.md §1)', but §1 is the graded $2.81/$3.55 run and $2.25 sits in the footnote.

The value unit is still open (D-23, COST_MODEL.md §5), and there is no scenario showing whether ~15-17 M tokens a month (Haiku era; OPERATING_TERMS.md §c), let alone the roughly 2x suggested by routing-validate-01, fits a subscription window. The usage-versus-labour side of the value claim therefore has no unit and no measured size under the routing actually in use.
scores.to_reach_9: Add a pilot investment and net-return section. It should give role-by-role hours for the 4 weeks, operator time and the usage/seat placeholder tied to T-02. It should set these against the reconciled EUR 4.0-4.2k floor, net of Tier 5-7 role minutes, with a stated break-even. Add a week-1 baseline protocol for downstream rework and client revision rounds on the six retro projects, so the pilot at least baselines the 'prize'. Fix the TIERS.md status contradiction and the stale OPERATING_TERMS citations. Once T-02 has run, add the measured current-routing tokens per brief to README's measured/assumed table.

scores.evidence:
The pilot pack is unusually complete for an MVP. docs/pilot/PILOT_RUNBOOK.md is a genuine one-page card: preflight, 5 steps with owner and time budget, exact commands, an exit-code routing table and a 'Never' list. ROLES.md is a RACI with exactly one A per row, backups, separation-of-duties rules and scorecard columns per role. GO_LIVE_DECISIONS.md lists 6 closed owner decisions and 26 open ones, each with owner, default-until-decided and deadline, plus technical preconditions T-01 to T-06. OPERATING_TERMS.md sets out account options A/B/C, the fixture-boundary blast radius and a ready-to-paste rule 4a. INCIDENT_RECOVERY.md covers 6 incident classes with commands and proposed time bounds. SCORECARD.md defines measures precisely (Levenshtein survival, 4-class question precision, CE1-CE5, manual fallback) with per-phase pass and stop rules. DATA_PROTECTION.md gives DPIA inputs.

I verified the pack against code. Runner exit codes 2, 4, 5 and 6 exist (pipeline/runner.py lines 38-45). intake requires --tier and --data-class with approval fields (intake.py 245-251). agency init requires --profile and --actor (agency.py 359-363). The --solo-rehearsal waiver is refused for non-synthetic data (agency.py 52-67; delivery.py 114-136). eval/pilot_scorecard.py implements pass/fail/insufficient_data per phase and treats missing data as never a pass (lines 98-244). The deterministic suite is green at 948 passed. runs/rehearsal-lifecycle/TRANSCRIPT.md walks the governance path in 37 steps.

The gaps are in what an agency needs on the day of approval. The routing the pilot would run has never produced a complete brief. The quality precondition T-03 is open with 16 documented defects. The only transport may not be usable under the required data terms. The approval path has only been rehearsed on patched renders.
defects: The pilot routing is unmeasured end to end. T-02 is open (GO_LIVE_DECISIONS.md line 55). Only one transcript leg has been measured, at 598 743 tokens against 295 774 (COST_MODEL.md §3). D-05 (seats/window/fee) and D-17 (refusal target) both default to 'size from T-02', so on approval day the agency cannot size its account or know its expected refusal and repair rate.

The quality precondition T-03 is open with no plan. SCORECARD.md's preamble requires tests/test_regression_voreas.py to pass with no xfail on regenerated artifacts. Today 16 strict xfails pin CE1-CE4-class defects (dropped objective, asserted resolution, misattributed or uncited claims, invented figure) against a scorecard target of 0 critical errors. No owner date or remediation path beyond 'next round' is given.

D-06 is a possible day-1 blocker with no contingency. pipeline/agents.py runs only through `claude -p`, and OPERATING_TERMS.md §c says option B 'needs a transport built' and that it is unknown whether the CLI can bill an API account. If the DPA, zero-retention and EU-processing terms (D-03) are only available on an API account, there is no scoped fallback: no effort estimate, and no note that building it needs a CLAUDE.md rule-4 owner decision.

The path from a model-generated render to approval has never been exercised. The lifecycle rehearsal patched the stored renders to add per-question [source_id location] tags (runs/rehearsal-lifecycle/TRANSCRIPT.md, 'render_patch'; regenerate.py line 199). The render-stage gates (pipeline/stages.py check_render and check_render_template) do not run quality.render_coverage's per-question linked-evidence check, which runs only at `agency approve` (pipeline/agency.py line 195). A live brief can therefore exit 0 and then be refused at approval. That case is not in PILOT_RUNBOOK.md or INCIDENT_RECOVERY.md.

Three things a sponsor needs are missing. There is no pilot report template, although the sponsor signs it (ROLES.md line 12; SCORECARD.md §5). There is no weekly checkpoint cadence (end of week 1 assumption validation, end of week 3 go/no-go meeting). And there is no per-role time commitment for the 4 weeks, so management cannot release people or judge the pilot's burden on billable staff.

Week-1 glossary building has no procedure. PRD §8 calls co-building the per-client glossary with the leads 'adoption lever #1', but intake only scaffolds {client_id, sensitivity_tier, terms}. No pilot doc explains how leads build and approve protected terms or what a good entry looks like.

The runbook's exit-code table is incomplete. PILOT_RUNBOOK.md omits exit 3 `pending_stage` (runner.py lines 40 and 766) and the outcomes `corrupt_artifact` (line 560) and `demo_profile_error` (line 643) that exit 4 can carry, so a champion reading the manifest has no routing for them.
scores.to_reach_9: Run the authorised current-routing re-baseline and publish per-brief tokens by model, wall time and refusal/repair rates. That closes T-02 and lets D-05 and D-17 be set from data. Give T-03 an owner, a date and a remediation route. Add the per-question tag check to the render stage for new renders, so a missing tag is repaired inside the run, and add the 'approve refused on render coverage' route to the runbook. Scope a D-06 contingency. Add a pilot report template, a weekly sponsor checkpoint and a per-role time commitment table. Add a week-1 glossary-building guide. Complete the exit-code table.

moves.title: Run the authorised current-routing re-baseline and close T-02 (and test T-03)
moves.rationale: The biggest reason the pilot cannot start on approval day is that the routing it would run has never produced a complete brief. Seats and window (D-05), the refusal target (D-17) and the usage side of the value claim all wait on it. The owner has already authorised it (OPERATING_DECISIONS.md 2026-09-22, decision 1).
moves.concrete_changes: Run 3 graded rolls each on fixtures/northlight_01 and fixtures/voreas_02 under the unchanged config/model_routing.json. Keep every roll, refused ones included. Report per-brief tokens by model with `python3 eval/cost_report.py`, and pass rates with eval pass-rate tooling (grade read-only via eval/grade_frozen.py, never the harness CLI). Rerun tests/test_regression_voreas.py against the regenerated voreas artifacts and record which xfails clear, without removing marks by hand. Update COST_MODEL.md §3, README.md table line 48, GO_LIVE_DECISIONS.md T-02/T-03/D-05/D-17 defaults, SCORECARD.md line 17 and OPERATING_TERMS.md §c with measured figures and era labels. Update WALKTHROUGH sheet 10 only after the owner has seen the numbers.

moves.title: Add a pilot investment and net-return sheet
moves.rationale: A managing director signs off risk and return. The repo gives a reconciled return floor (EUR 4.0-4.2k/yr) but never says what the pilot costs in staff hours and usage, so there is no break-even and no way to judge whether the pilot is worth running.
moves.concrete_changes: Create docs/pilot/PILOT_INVESTMENT.md with: (a) a per-role hours table for weeks 1-4, derived from ROLES.md activities and PILOT_RUNBOOK.md time budgets (assembly <=20, review <30, verdict 2, record 2 minutes per brief x 6 retro + N live briefs, plus week-1 validation and glossary sessions, champion training T-06, and the sponsor and DPO decision sessions); (b) the operator/AI-specialist time; (c) a seat/usage placeholder tied to T-02; (d) cost at PRD A4 EUR 19-20/h for account staff, with other roles' rates marked OWNER TO CONFIRM; (e) break-even in briefs against the EUR 38-40 per brief floor; (f) an explicit statement that the downstream 'prize' is unpriced. Link it from README.md 'What is measured and what is assumed' as an Assumption row, and from GO_LIVE_DECISIONS.md.

moves.title: Net the Tier 5-7 role minutes out of capacity returned
moves.rationale: The capacity formula counts only account-lead minutes. The agency layer adds attester, traffic, creative-lead, champion and operator minutes, so the published return can be overstated. The pilot scorecard should report net team minutes next to lead minutes.
moves.concrete_changes: SCORECARD.md §3 'Capacity returned': add a reported-only net measure, (baseline_min - total_team_min) where team components are measured, with a team baseline captured on retro rows (a new `baseline_team_min` column in scorecard_template.csv, recalled per role, same method as A1). eval/pilot_scorecard.py: add a reported (non-gating) `net_team_minutes` rule that returns insufficient_data unless every component is measured. Add a test in tests/ covering the missing-component and exact-value cases. Mirror the formula in COST_MODEL.md §4. No existing pass rule changes.

moves.title: Baseline downstream rework on the six retro projects in week 1
moves.rationale: The documents say the case rests on the variance floor and downstream rework, yet the pilot scores neither and leaves the baseline 'OWNER TO CONFIRM' (D-19). The six retrospective projects already have known outcomes, so their creative rework requests and client revision rounds can be baselined cheaply now instead of waiting for quarter 1.
moves.concrete_changes: SCORECARD.md §5 week 1: add a step in which traffic and the account leads pull `creative_rework_requests_q1` and `client_revision_rounds_q1` for each retro project from existing traffic and account logs and record them on the retro rows as the historical baseline (reported, not gated). GO_LIVE_DECISIONS.md D-19: change the default from 'Not pilot-scored' to 'Baseline recorded on retro rows in week 1; comparison in quarter 1'. PRD stays untouched.

moves.title: Enforce the approval-time question-tag contract inside the render stage
moves.rationale: quality.render_coverage's per-question linked-evidence check runs only at `agency approve`. The rehearsal patched renders to satisfy it, so a live brief can exit 0 and then be refused at approval. Moving the same check, unloosened, into the render stage for newly generated renders lets the existing single repair attempt fix it inside the run. This tightens a gate; it does not relax one.
moves.concrete_changes: pipeline/stages.py check_render_template: also call the question-block portion of quality.render_coverage for new renders (historical renders stay audited by check_render, unchanged). Add tests/test_stages.py cases: a render missing a question's [source_id location] tag fails the render gate; a correct one passes. Add a row to the PILOT_RUNBOOK.md exit table and a section to INCIDENT_RECOVERY.md: 'agency approve refused on render coverage -> `--stage render` on the same run ID'. Regenerate runs/rehearsal-lifecycle with a note on whether render_patch is still needed.

moves.title: Sponsor pack: pilot report template, checkpoint cadence, role time commitments
moves.rationale: The sponsor signs a pilot report that has no template. There is no weekly decision rhythm and no statement of how much time each role must give, which is what management needs to release people on the day of approval.
moves.concrete_changes: Create docs/pilot/PILOT_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md with sections mapped one-to-one to `eval/pilot_scorecard.py --output` fields: pass_rules per phase, fallbacks, CE counts, adoption, incidents from $PILOT/incidents.jsonl, A1/A2/A4 as validated in week 1, and capacity recomputed from them. Add a 'Checkpoints' table to PILOT_RUNBOOK.md or SCORECARD.md §5: kickoff (D-01 closed), end of week 1 (assumptions validated, glossary approved), end of week 3 (go/no-go on the six retro rows), end of week 4 (report). Add a 'Time commitment (weeks 1-4)' column to the ROLES.md roles table.

moves.title: Close day-1 operating gaps: D-06 contingency, glossary guide, full exit table
moves.rationale: Three small gaps would stall a champion or the operator in week 1. There is no fallback if the data terms force an API account, no procedure for the glossary the PRD calls adoption lever #1, and some runner outcomes have no routing.
moves.concrete_changes: (1) OPERATING_TERMS.md §c: add a 'If only option B carries the required terms' paragraph. It should scope an API transport behind pipeline/agents.py's existing seam, give an effort estimate, and state that it needs a CLAUDE.md rule-4 amendment (owner) with defaults until then. Link it from GO_LIVE_DECISIONS.md D-06. (2) New docs/pilot/GLOSSARY_BUILDING.md: how leads fill `terms` in the intake scaffold (protected brand terms, EN marketing terms kept in Latin script, per-client do-not-translate items), who approves them, and how they are versioned. Synthetic example only. (3) PILOT_RUNBOOK.md exit table: add exit 3 `pending_stage` and the exit-4 outcomes `corrupt_artifact` and `demo_profile_error`, with actions.

moves.title: Truth pass on TIERS status line and OPERATING_TERMS citations
moves.rationale: These are cheap contradictions that undermine trust in a record that is otherwise very careful: TIERS.md says no Tier 8 is authorised while carrying a green Tier 8, and OPERATING_TERMS cites line numbers and sections that have drifted.
moves.concrete_changes: docs/TIERS.md lines 6-8: restate the status as 'Tiers 0-8 complete and green; Tier 8 is round 1 of the owner's review loop (authorised 2026-09-22)'. docs/pilot/OPERATING_TERMS.md §b and §e: replace 'docs/TIERS.md line 55' and 'CLAUDE.md ... line 55' with phrase citations ('Session & budget plan, internal engineering note'; 'Workflow'). In §c, replace '$2.25 (docs/COST_MODEL.md §1)' with '(docs/COST_MODEL.md, dollar footnote)'. Add a test or grep in scripts/check.sh that flags 'line NN' citations to other docs in docs/pilot/.

overall: The honesty and preparation here are above what I usually see from a vendor or an internal team. Measured figures are separated from assumptions, the inflated PRD return is corrected in the open, every open decision has an owner and a default, and the runbook, RACI, incident procedures and scorecard are backed by code I verified. I would still not sign go-live today, for two reasons. First, the return case has no cost side and does not test the value it says matters most. Second, the pilot would run on a routing that has never produced a complete brief, with an open quality precondition carrying 16 documented critical-error-class defects, a transport that may not fit the required data terms, and an approval path rehearsed only on patched renders. Both aspects score 7. Running the authorised re-baseline and adding a pilot investment and net-return sheet would move them most.
